source.title: Machine Unlearning of Pre-trained Large Language Models
source.authors: Jin Yao; Eli Chien; Min-Xin Du; Xinyao Niu; Tianhao Wang; Ze-Zhou Cheng; Xiang Yue

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates unlearning methods on pre-trained Yi-6B and measures performance on the forget set and downstream tasks, but it does not test recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper tests removal-oriented methods and reports forget-set accuracy and perplexity. It does not test fine-tuning recovery, activation edits, quantization, or prompting attacks. MIA results concern membership inference, not recovery of targeted knowledge. Results cited from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: It applies seven gradient-based unlearning methods to pre-training data of Yi-6B (arXiv, GitHub, Books). It reports forget-set accuracy and perplexity plus downstream utility, which bears on the first half of A. It runs no recovery attacks, so B–F and A's attack-resistance part are untested. Its target is approximate-retrain (unseen-data) level, not chance.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say the seven adapted methods effectively unlearn pre-training data at about 10^5 times less compute than retraining, judged against an approximate-retrain target. They find GA + descent on in-distribution data more robust to hyperparameters, and give tuning guidelines. They note utility costs for some methods on code and that current MIA methods struggle. MIA AUC near 0.5 holds only for arXiv, not GitHub or Books.
record.recipe_differences: Adapts several approximate unlearning methods, including gradient ascent, to next-token prediction on pre-training data; uses Yi-6B and copyright-related corpora. It does not test the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that outcomes vary with learning rate, optimization steps, batch size, forget-set size, and the type of retained data; gradient ascent plus in-distribution descent is described as more stable.

fits_no_version.finding: Min-K% MIA AUC falls after unlearning. arXiv stays near 0.5 (50.77→~50.3); GitHub goes 81.93→74.28–80.55; Books goes 74.03→56.39–69.81.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-based unlearning of pre-training sequences lowers but does not remove membership-inference detectability.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: Experiments focus on one model, Yi-6B. Retraining is approximated using unseen same-domain data, not the full retained corpus. No chance-level accuracy reference is given. The paper notes that membership-inference methods struggle to distinguish members from non-members. Some table values are flattened in the supplied text, and the Books experiment description says 500 books whereas Table 3 says 100 books.
record.rows_left_out: Downstream-task table values beyond the HumanEval declines stated in the text were not assigned to individual methods because the supplied table layout does not unambiguously map all values. Additional retain-set metrics and detailed downstream task scores are in Tables 1–3; hyperparameter sweeps are in Figures 2–3.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks (fine-tuning, prompting, quantization, probing) recover the forgotten content; a chance-level target (methods are tuned to unseen-data level instead).
All: no activation edits or access-vs-deletion analysis.
All: no rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context probes.
All: no method is evaluated against recovery attacks.

missing.what: Downstream MMLU/ARC/GSM8K/avg scores per method. Utility is mostly preserved on arXiv and Books (avg within ~1.2 of 45.48); GitHub GA+descent-indist avg is 40.63.
Hyperparameter sweeps. Higher learning rate or more steps send forget/general perplexity up to ~10^30 and collapse downstream accuracy for all methods except GA+descent-indist.
Three-seed means and SDs for the GitHub results.

record.verdict_notes: All row versions were 'V1' (invalid). The reader's 'challenges' label for A is not justified, because the paper deliberately targets unseen-data level rather than chance. The study never probes recovery, so it says nothing on shallowness. Single model (Yi-6B), one epoch.

versions.untested_parts: Whether simple attacks recover knowledge after unlearning; the paper does not test recovery attacks. It evaluates targeted-data performance and general downstream ability, but does not establish a chance-level reference.
Fine-tuning to recover knowledge using unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten examples.
Activation-direction ablation or analysis of access-blocking versus deletion.
Recovery through rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
A newer method resisting the listed recovery attacks.

relationships.condition: Forget-set next-token accuracy after all seven methods, arXiv/GitHub/Books, Yi-6B, LR tuned to approximate-retrain target
relationships.reason: Accuracy drops only to around unseen-data level, far from chance (GitHub 80.65→75.09–78.79; Books 55.26→50.07–52.85; arXiv 69.02→~68.8). This is by design, since the target is retrain level (github-acc-*, books-acc-*, arxiv-acc-* method rows).
relationships.display_finding: Tuning toward approximate retraining reduced GitHub accuracy from 80.65 to 75.09–78.79, Books from 55.26 to 50.07–52.85 and arXiv from 69.02 to approximately 68.8.

source_check.condition: Forget-set next-token accuracy after all seven methods, arXiv/GitHub/Books, Yi-6B, LR tuned to approximate-retrain target
source_check.reason: Numbers are right (Tables 1-3). But the study sets the LR so each method reaches the approximate-retrain (unseen-data) level, not chance. Ending above chance is a design choice, so A's near-chance part is untested, and untested parts are not limits_scope.

relationships.display_finding: HumanEval fell from 16.46 to 10.98 with random labels, 9.76 with adversarial samples and 2.44 with GA plus in-distribution descent.

relation.reason: Its forget-set accuracy/perplexity and downstream utility results (e.g. the HumanEval drop) bear on version A.

tranche.reason: New setting: gradient-based unlearning of Yi-6B pre-training data (arXiv, GitHub, Books). Its forget-set and downstream results bear on A; it runs no recovery attacks.

source_check.notes: All 20 values match Tables 1-3. The arXiv changes are small but in the right direction, and the authors call them a 'slight decline', not negligible, so partial fits. The text says 500 books, but the Table 3 caption and Table 4 say 100. HumanEval column mapping is confirmed by the Avg column and Table 6. Figure 2 and Appendix A show that higher LR, more steps or larger forget sets raise general-set PPL and cut downstream accuracy. No row captures this.
